parameters.content:
## Faceless YouTube Shorts on autopilot

Every morning this workflow picks a topic it has not covered yet, writes a short
script, voices it, finds matching stock footage, renders a captioned 1080x1920
video with Zvid and (optionally) uploads it to YouTube.

### Setup (about five minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Upload voiceover*, *Save draft to editor*, *Validate project*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **ElevenLabs** — add a SECOND **Header Auth** credential: name `xi-api-key`,
   value = your ElevenLabs key. Attach it to *Generate voiceover*. The key only
   needs text-to-speech permission.
3. **OpenRouter** (or any OpenAI-compatible chat API) — attach it to *Write script*.
4. **Open `Channel Config`** and set `niche`, `audience`, `channelHandle`, the
   `voiceId` and your brand colours. On a FREE ElevenLabs plan only default voices
   work — Voice Library voices return 402. Brian, George, Roger, Sarah and Bill are
   confirmed working; see the workflow README for their ids.
5. Run it once with `dryRun: true` (the default). No credits are charged — you get
   the exact cost plus an **editorLink** that opens the draft in the Zvid editor.
6. Set `dryRun: false` to render, and `uploadToYouTube: true` once you are happy.

### Cost per video

A thirty second 1080x1920 render is about **28-32 Zvid credits**. Free accounts
include enough to test. The script costs well under a cent; the voice uses about
400 ElevenLabs characters, so a free ElevenLabs tier covers roughly 25 videos.

## No stock media keys needed

`/api/stock/search` is Zvid's stock library — footage, photos and music behind one
endpoint with server-side keys, so there is nothing extra to sign up for and the
endpoint needs no authentication of its own.

**Portrait clips win.** The picker scores portrait footage highest because the
canvas is 1080x1920; a landscape clip still works through `resize: "cover"`, it is
just cropped harder.

**Music tags are single words.** The music catalogue matches tags rather than
phrases, so the writer is restricted to a list known to return results.

## Why transcribe a voice we just generated?

Text-to-speech returns audio but no timings. Transcribing it back gives the exact
start and end of every spoken word, which this workflow uses twice:

- **Cuts land on sentence boundaries** — each scene ends when its own sentence ends,
  instead of on an estimated average.
- **Captions are word-perfect** — the karaoke highlight tracks the real voice, which
  is the single biggest quality difference in short-form video.

If the word counts ever drift, the build step silently falls back to a proportional
split so a video is still produced.

## Dry run first — it is free

With `dryRun: true` the workflow stops here and saves the project as a **draft**,
then reports an **editorLink** like
`https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the video back, adjust anything by hand, and see the exact scene
timing before you spend a single credit. Saving a draft is free.

When the draft looks right, set `dryRun: false` in **Channel Config**.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow runs anywhere,
including n8n Cloud with nothing installed.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap them for native nodes:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

The Zvid Trigger removes the polling loop entirely.

## Publishing

`uploadToYouTube` is **false** by default so your first runs stay private. Turn it
on once the output looks right, and keep `youTubePrivacy` on `private` or
`unlisted` until you have watched a few.

The YouTube node needs a **YouTube OAuth2** credential (Google Cloud project with
the YouTube Data API enabled).

Swap this node for TikTok, Instagram or a Google Drive upload — everything before
it stays identical.
